chunks.content: 96 The Secret Weapon for Closing Deals (That Most Buyers Ignore) Hi Sara, Let’s be honest, most people looking to buy a business are focused on the tactical stuff: ✅ Getting the best purchase price ✅ Structuring the terms just right ✅ Finding a bank with the best rate But after years of working on deals, here’s the actual secret weapon to closing more of them: Empathy. No, it’s not just a mushy buzzword. It’s the most underutilized tool in the dealmaking toolkit. Especially when you're dealing with professional services firms, like accounting practices, where legacy, relationships, and emotions run deep. Buyers, I know it feels like you’ve poured everything into this deal. But guess what? So has the seller, just add a decade or six. This might be their life’s work. Their clients are like family. Their clients and employees might literally be family. So when they push back on that clause about benefit commitments or ask for a softer retention structure—pause before you assume bad faith. Likewise, sellers, if your buyer wants to renegotiate post due diligence, it doesn’t mean they’re trying to lowball you. They’re scared. They’re about to take on the biggest loan in their lives for something they’ve never run before. Empathy doesn’t mean caving. It means understanding what’s driving the other side’s concerns, and adjusting your strategy accordingly. If you approach your next deal with that mindset? You won’t just get better terms. You’ll actually get to closing. Want more behind-the-scenes deal psychology like this? Join me every week for sharp insights, no fluff. And if you missed this week’s video, it’s live now on YouTube.
